subject: Materials Science
title: Ionic and Covalent Crystal Structures
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ionic and Covalent Crystal Structures usable.

hook.text: Table salt cracks along flat planes. Diamond doesn't crack at all. Both are crystals — but bonded differently.

buildup.text: Ionic crystals pack positive and negative ions to maximize attraction and minimize repulsion.

discovery.text: NaCl has the rock salt structure — each ion surrounded by six of the opposite charge.

twist.text: Covalent crystals like SiC share electrons in rigid bonds — extremely hard but brittle.

climax.text: Silicon carbide's covalent structure makes it hard enough to cut steel and survive 1,600°C.

punchline.text: The bond type dictates the crystal and the crystal dictates the properties.

quiz.question: What determines the structure of an ionic crystal?
options: Maximizing attraction between opposite charges while minimizing repulsion
Sharing electrons equally between all atoms
